participants: Andrew Jin / Andrew Musial (closer, Primal Instinct)
summary: A one-to-one with almost no sales content. Andrew opens anxious about a five-day men's workshop he is leaving for the next day, and Chris redirects the whole session into consciousness and ego work - identity as programming, watching thoughts, fear of death, karma, souls, religion and the value of raising one's level of consciousness. Andrew discloses that he was in a bad place a few months ago, considered quitting everything, was financially strained and had to liquidate investments he had promised himself he would not touch in order to pay for coaching and mentorship. Chris connects the consciousness work back to closing in the last ten minutes, arguing that an open, egoless field is what actually produces high close rates, and recommends David Hawkins' Letting Go plus an invitation to meet his own spiritual teacher. He signs off by noting that he is still the sales manager and will still hold Andrew to his standards.
notable: Recording disclosure is made at the top - 'This meeting is being recorded' - the only explicit disclosure in the batch.

The manager conducts extended personal and spiritual work with a direct report and recommends his personal teacher; he then reasserts the performance relationship in the same call. Flagged separately.

Stated closing philosophy that a principal should see: 'every single person has a buyer inside of them... I'm just going to help them remove whatever in their brain is telling them that they can't be their best, because I know it's just their ego. And when you get really good at talking to your ego, you can talk to anyone's ego.' Flagged separately.

Andrew discloses personal financial distress and that he liquidated investments to buy coaching - directly relevant context for how he handles prospects in the same position, which he encountered twice in this batch.
Chris frames sales as 'the transference of energy' and claims his own field lifts prospects 'whether they close or not' - the same certainty-transfer language used in the 06/15 training block.
Andrew is out for five days from this date, which explains the gap in his call volume at the end of the batch window.
